Messages.Author: legb...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
i made this deck with the contents of just over two boxes of Jyhad
boosters, plus cards i have won in tourneys. i've already built two
remarkably competitive decks from this pool - Nosferatu "Kagemusha"
Happy Families deck, and Anam and Ian's wedding deck. This one used the
leftovers, and positively STORMED to victory just now against Sarah's HF
Ravnos and Michael's Anklebiter Goes Tactical deck. At the end i
actually had over 30 pool, 6 vampires [1 in torpor], 2 outcast mages,
loyal street gang, Arms dealer, Thadius Zho and a renegade garou armed
with the assault rifle!

CRYPT [15 vampires]
2 x Igo the Hungry
Dre, Leader of the Cold dawn
Roreca Quaid
Uma Hatch
Dr John Casey
Rake
Giuliano Vincenzi
Lydia van Cuelen
Lupo
Angel
Vliam Andor
Anastasia Grey
Jing Wei
Ricki van Demsy

LIBRARY [90 cards]

MASTERS [18]
Ascendance x 8
The Barrens
Effective Management x 3
Information Highway
Misdirection x 3
Presence x 2

DISCIPLINELESS [63]
Arms Dealer x 2
Assault Rifle
Autarkis Persecution x 7
Bribes x 5
Brujah Justicar
Change of Target x 2
Computer Hacking x 10
Cryptic Rider
Dramatic Upheaval
The Embrace x 2
Praxis Seizure: Chicago
Praxis Seizure: Cleveland
Praxis Seizure: Dallas
Praxis Seizure: Seattle
Kine Resources Contested
Lucky Blow x 4
Conservative Agitation x 4
Outcast Mage x 2
Renegade Garou x 3
Thadius Zho [Mage]
Tremere Justicar x 2
The Knights
Loyal Street gang x 2
Fake Out x 4
Zip Gun x 3

PRESENCE [9]
Bewitching Oration x 4
Charming Lobby
Disarming Presence x 2
Dread Gaze
Legal Manipulations

i actually didn't play ANY presence cards in this game, so they are
probably questionable - i shall keep them at least until i've tested the
deck in bigger/more competitive games. Lucky Blows might be better as
extra fake Outs, dodges or Flak/leather jackets. Autarkis Persecution
and recruiting allies worked a treat, misdirection and computer hacking
and change of target all working smoothly together in their usual way.
Could probably lose an effective management or two and thereby find
space for SR and KRCG NEws Radio. Ascendance is GREAT in this deck. Not
hard to devise a strategy to beat this deck, of course, but it does
demonstrate that you can build a decent deck out of cheap and/or sucky
cards.

Messages.Author: legb...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
i used the above deck again for our Monday night playgroup games, twice.
In the first [a 3-player] i got pretty much slaughtered by my predator
John Eagles but then we both got rubbed out by Louisa. In the second [ a
4-player] i swept, but it was a VERY tough and interesting game. Mike
[Louisa's boyfriend, and a new player] ALMOST got me by stealth-bleed but
vigorous top-decking JUST got me the Autarkis Persecution i needed to
stay alive. This game actually saw TWO assault rifles hit the table - one
mine, in the hands of a renegade garou, and the other John's and weilded
by Anton [Bauble on Wendy Wade]. So i rushed and ate Wendy to get rid of
his one, and then gunned down a couple of war ghouls. GREAT fun! i made
one change to the deck - Delilah Easton for one of the Igos.

Messages.Author: Derek Ray
Messages.Body:
On Tue, 24 Oct 2000 12:15:46 -0400, Marc Gabriele
<goo...@dementia.org> wrote:



I'm sure it does. The list of consequences you mentioned is there
simply to clarify the obvious - that when a vampire goes away,
everything on him of course goes away as well.

But that doesn't include the equipment, which is on another vampire.

In a "how is this happening?" sense, a vamp with Vicissitude basically
turns ITSELF into the equipment and then gives itself to another
vampire to use. So the left-over vampire doesn't even really "exist",
in one sense - represented by "can't take actions, block, or vote."
(CAN play Telepathic Counter/Misdirection, however, and can Rat's
Warning to do the same.) But you can't remove the vampire from the
game, since it can always be turned back INTO a vampire... and so, the
"burn" clause on Bauble and why beating up the "non-existent" vampire
doesn't actually affect the equipment.

This also lends itself to a nasty little deck idea with the
Brujah/Toreador, involving as many itty bitty cel/pre vampires as you
can manage, VIC skill cards, and Assault Rifles out the wazoo. Bleed
with Legal Manipulations, toss some Blur cards in there for the poor
souls who get in your way, and toss some Flash in to be -sure- you
stay away. And the biggest problem would be somehow being sure you
could get the VIC card, THEN the Bauble, and not getting any ARs in
your hand in the meantime. =)

Or you could just include Christine Boscacci, Horatio, and
Rex-the-not-quite-useless in your crypt in sufficient numbers. Then
you can remove the VIC skill cards and do something useful with the
master slots you've saved (and also have a much better hope of getting
the Bauble before the AR.)

Messages.Author: legb...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
i won again with this deck on Wednesday night, taking 4/6 VP from a
6-player game. My victims were, in order, Philip playing Tremere [he IS
a new guy, and to his credit he wasn't trying to play Tremere combat],
John Keech playing presence-dominate vote, deflect and bleed, Garry
playing dom/pro/for and MArk playing his notorious stonewall deck -
aus/obf/dom with a bit of presence, vote, deflect and counter. i don't
know if i would have got John Eagles - he was decked but still had a
fair number of permanents and some pool, whereas i was down to 3 rather
weedy minions. One of them was the Garou, so i suppose i would have,
eventually.

This deck really surprises me by its robustness. The individual
components [allies, wee vamps and not-very-stealthy votes] are weak and
fragile but overall the deck is amazingly tough. i'm sure there's the
basis of something a bit more poky in this.
